memories.content: The user used an accessible entrance at a clinic in December 2024.
On a day snow had accumulated and blocked the main-entrance ramp, the user went to a side entrance.
The user learned on site that the elevator was under inspection and delayed the appointment.
The day before the next visit, the user called to check whether the elevator would be operating.
The user waited for their turn in front of a ticket machine near the waiting chairs.
On a day the user waited in a corridor without chairs, they leaned against the wall and changed position several times.
On a day their older sister accompanied them, the user found a place to sit immediately after reception.
Reception staff expect that a first-time visitor may ask where the accessible entrance is.
The local agent cannot infer the user's condition from a record of using an accessible route alone.
Snow accumulation and snow-removal work can temporarily block an entrance route used under ordinary conditions.
The user collects clothes for donation in a large bag beside the entrance.
After emptying an entire drawer at once, the user could not find a charger they needed.
During the next organizing session, the user sorted items by type and put only items to be discarded in the bag.
Even after photographing unworn clothes, the user did not take them out again for one month.
After moving those clothes to the donation bag, the user cleared one closet compartment.
The user nearly discarded an important paper with advertising and checked the recycling box again.
During the next organizing session, the user kept a separate document box and did not mix the papers.
The user's mother asks the user to check whether she needs kitchen items in good condition before discarding them.
Confirm with the user before marking a personal document or another person's property as a disposal candidate.
The local agent cannot determine an object's emotional meaning from frequency of use alone.

analysis.overview: The frames cover unrelated domains: the reference describes clinic accessibility, waiting, and inference limits, while the compared frame describes household organizing, disposal safeguards, and meaning-assessment limits. No claims address the same operational decision closely enough to form a cross-frame relation.
